newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN-Iraq oil deal overseers to arrive at UN Monday.
newsitem.headline: UN-Iraq oil deal overseers to arrive at UN Monday.

text.p: United Nations appointed oil overseers will arrive here Monday in time for the start of oil contract sales under the newly implemented oil-for-food accord, a U.N. spokesman said.
He spokesman said the four overseers will assemble ahead of the Tuesday 0501 GMT start time, as dictated by terms of the May 20 arrangement.
"They will be here on Monday for the start," he said.
The overseers must review all oil contracts submitted by Iraq within 24 hours.
The U.N. said earlier Monday that U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali approved the accord, issuing a "final report" to the president of the U.N. Security Council.

Under terms of the deal, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude oil over six months, which is renewable, to buy food and supplies for civilians suffering from sanctions imposed after Baghdad invaded Kuwait in August 1990.

The deal also stipulates that nearly two-thirds, or about $1.3 million of the total oil revenues, are earmarked for needy Iraqis, with the balance to pay for Gulf war reparations and other monitoring costs.
A team of 14 people from the the Dutch-firm Saybolt are in Iraq, charged with monitoring outflows of Iraqi oil at three border stations.
A separate team of 32 people from Lloyd's Register will be at import facilities in Iraq to ensure only prescribed supplies are brought into the country.
In addition, more than 150 U.N. distribution monitors will work in the country to make sure the food and aid gets to those intended.
